selectedPhrase: ما العمل في أيام العشر أفضل من العمل في هذه

printedEvidence.observation: Contains the ten-days comparison with the same direction; uses منه and expands the first jihad question with في سبيل الله. Matching core wording is not independent confirmation that this variant is preferred.
Contains the selected comparison clause. The chapter introduction follows a different Quran-quotation form from the digital source.

commentary.author: Ibn Hajar al-‘Asqalani
commentary.locator: Book of the Two Eids · chapter on deeds during the days of Tashriq · discussion beginning قوله: ما العمل في أيام
commentary.finding: Identifies this wording with Karimah’s transmission from al-Kushmihani, calls that form anomalous, and contrasts it with other transmitted forms. The issue concerns the wording variant, not a blanket rejection of the underlying hadith.
commentary.shortArabicQuotation: والسياق الذي وقع في رواية كريمة شاذ

bewley.observation: Its any-ten-days wording is not a literal equivalent of the selected definite ten-days clause.

khan.observation: Uses other days versus these and supplies a parenthetical identifying the first ten days. This cannot silently replace or translate away the selected Arabic variant.

decision.reason: A material disputed wording cannot be settled by counting matching editions or by copying a smoother English comparison.
decision.nextWork: Inspect an additional identified Arabic edition and its variant apparatus, then prepare a source-selection decision for qualified review. Preserve this input and all variant evidence. Do not ask the user to adjudicate the Arabic meaning.
